<issue>
httrack <URL> --build-top-index exits 255 with the usage screen instead of crawling
Any option whose expansion contains a lowercase `i` is mistaken for `-i` (continue) when it appears after the URL. The URL list is wiped and httrack prints the usage screen:

```
$ httrack http://example.com/ -O /tmp/d --build-top-index ; echo $?
(usage screen)
255
```

In `htscoremain.c` the pass that counts URLs also detects `-i`. For anything `cmdl_opt()` calls an option it runs `strchr(tmp_argv[0], 'i')` and sets `argv_url = -1` on a match. That test happens after `optalias_check()` has expanded the long aliases, so `--build-top-index` becomes `-%i` and `--protocol N` becomes `-@iN`, and both match the bare letter. `argv_url` ends up at 0, no URL survives, and the run reaches the usage screen. The same value also means "reload `hts-cache/doit.log`" further down, so inside an existing project directory this resumes the previous crawl instead of failing.

Argument order changes how visible the failure is, but the option is misparsed either way. Placed before the URL, `-%i` still sets `opt->quiet = 1`, which is the other half of the `-i` handling; the URL that follows resets the counter and the crawl then proceeds normally.

I instrumented both `strchr` sites and confirmed the matches at runtime. `-%i` / `--build-top-index` and `-@iN` / `--protocol N` are affected. The neighbouring `strchr(tmp_argv[0], 'q')` has the same bug, where `-%q` / `--include-query-string` quietly turns on quiet mode.

Filters such as `+*.gif` are unaffected, since `cmdl_opt()`'s `*`, `.` and `/` heuristic keeps them out of the option branch. `-i`, `-iC1`, `-iC2`, `--continue` and `--update` are all meant to wipe the URL list, so their current behaviour is correct and should stay.


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.
